tips.text: Montenegro uses the standard European plate with a blue strip, and the Montenegro coat of arms on a **red circle**. The red circle is visible through the blur. NOTE: The white section of Albanian licence plates do not have a red circle.

All Generation 4 coverage in Montenegro was taken using a “smallcam” camera, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot. NOTE: Most of the Balkans and southern Europe have Smallcam.

Montenegro is a small, **mountainous** country. Inland mountains are lush and green, while most coastal mountains have distinct exposed, light coloured rock. Most roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide.
The most common bollard is white with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back. The bollard also has a black top. NOTE: These bollards are also found in Slovenia.
Montenegro uses **black on white** or **red on yellow** chevrons. NOTE: Albania uses white on black chevrons.

Montenegro is the only Balkan country where you’ll commonly see both [A-type](https://goo.gl/maps/fZCnn3jPH4By45ph7) and [B-type](https://goo.gl/maps/w9hnQsjxxJS2TbT1A) guardrails. NOTE: For a good overview of European guardrails, see [this infographic](/images/montenegro/europeguardrail.png).
Montenegro uses simple **round concrete** or wooden poles.
‘**Rifts**’ can uncommonly be seen in Montenegrin generation 3 coverage, due to poor stitching. NOTE: Rifts are also common in Albania, and can rarely be seen in various other countries.

regional_clues.text: Although rifts are common in generation 3 Montenegro coverage, coastal rounds **will almost never **have them. By the coast, there will be a [short antenna](https://goo.gl/maps/d7Fvp2NzZw37CxyFA) with no rifts. There will be a [long antenna](https://goo.gl/maps/Zpu6fUJ5o3LkTtxZ6) with rifts inland. NOTE: An exception to this is the area around the coastal villages of Utjeha and Dobra Voda.
Green, **agricultural valleys** with deforested hills to make way for farmland are most commonly seen in the north.
The Bay of Kotor has a **touristy and populated** feel to it, with many people dressed in swimwear. A distinct [steep, rocky ridge](https://goo.gl/maps/Sj5ENoJMcprLyLzWA) can also be seen.
**Dry mountains** with a lack of trees are seen around Podgorica, and to the south of it. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.
**Pine forests** can be found in the north and a small area north of Nikšić, but most commonly in the **east**.

Durmitor National Park can be recognized by a distinct landscape consisting of **grassy, treeless mountains** with a high-altitude feel. The town of [Žabljak](https://goo.gl/maps/ityFp93bD3WQweCq5) is situated in this national park, and can be recognized by the landscape but also by the [unique](https://goo.gl/maps/1dyUEW1YaCgDS1SU9) [architecture](https://goo.gl/maps/wQFbfwF88LLTbie77).

spotlights.text: Podgorica is the capital and **largest city** in Montenegro, and can be recognized by the modern buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.
These distinct **staircase-like** mountainsides can be seen in the Cemi River Valley.
Many small islands can be seen within **Slansko Lake**.
The Pljevlja Coal Mine can be recognized by the wide, artificial **wall of gravel**. The mine can often be seen from [afar](https://goo.gl/maps/45CwG7nnsD9NjzXE6).
The Skadar Lake Bridge can be recognized by the **railway** and stone bollards next to the road.
